how_it_behaves: A small white calculator window is centred on a black background in Basic mode. It has a light-grey history pane above a white input line with a caret, and a keypad below with an orange = button on the right. Evaluating moves the entered expression, an = sign and the bold result onto the lowest line of the grey history pane and leaves the result in the white input line; multiplication is displayed as × and division as ÷, including immediately when * or / are typed, so the input line will not read back literally with * or / characters.

skills.name: ensure_calculator_ready
skills.does: Confirm the Basic calculator window is visible and ready for input.

steps.question: Is the white Basic calculator window showing, with a light-grey history pane above a white input line and a keypad below that includes an orange = button at the lower right?
steps.why: Calculation must not start until the calculator is on screen.

skills.name: clear_calculator
skills.does: Clear any previous expression or result from the calculator input.

steps.target: the C button, the first button in the top row of the keypad directly below the white input line, to the left of the ( button

steps.question: Is the white input line below the grey history pane empty, showing only a text caret?
steps.why: A leftover expression or result must not contaminate the new calculation.

skills.name: calculate
skills.does: Type an input expression, evaluate it with Return, and read back and verify the displayed answer.

inputs.expression: the arithmetic expression to calculate, using keyboard characters such as digits, parentheses, +, -, * and /

steps.target: the white expression input line directly below the light-grey history pane and above the keypad, identifiable by the text caret at its left end

steps.question: Is the white input line showing the expression {expression}, allowing multiplication to be displayed as × instead of * and division as ÷ instead of /?
steps.why: The calculator converts * and / to × and ÷ as they are typed, so the literal read-back check on typing must be skipped and this visual check, which accepts the converted symbols, catches any mistyped expression before evaluating it.

steps.question: Has the lowest line of the light-grey history pane become a completed calculation with an = sign and a bold result at its right end, while the white input line below shows a result?
steps.why: Confirm Return evaluated the expression instead of leaving it uncalculated or going elsewhere.

fields.answer: the value in the white input line directly below the grey history pane and above the C button row, at the left with the text caret immediately after it; this is not the bold value in the grey pane above
fields.history_result: the bold value at the right-hand end of the lowest completed line in the light-grey history pane, on the same line as the = sign and above the white input line

target.name: Calculator
target.suggested_goal: Work out the expression given in the inputs using the calculator's own buttons, and report the answer shown on screen.
